findings.message: Change 041 is a delivery-module change, but it still edits platform code and deletes a platform module. It adds `ModuleManifest.nav` and `ScreenProps.searchParams` in packages/core and a new packages/core/tests/registry.test.ts. It reworks the nav and route mounting in apps/web (registry.ts, profile.ts, Shell.tsx, [module]/[[...path]]/page.tsx). It edits packages/ui (the PinButton/IntentButton icon and shell.css `.me` padding). It deletes modules/hello. The module standard says a module change touches only `modules/<name>/` plus one CODEOWNERS line, and that `packages/` and `apps/web` belong to the platform team. Fix: split the nav[]/searchParams contract, the shell/IntentButton/`.me` changes and the hello removal into a platform-lane change that 041 depends on, and keep 041 to modules/delivery.
findings.scenario: git diff --stat main...041 → files under packages/core, packages/ui, apps/web and modules/hello change in a lane-'delivery' change; the boundary rule is broken

findings.message: The 'Tasks done per week' chart has its y-axis fixed at `max={40}`. Any week with more than 40 planned or done tasks is drawn above the plot area (`.chart{overflow:visible}`) against the 40 gridline, so the chart misreports the value. ProposalsPage already sizes its bar chart from the data, so the two charts behave differently. Fix: derive max from the series, e.g. `Math.max(40, ceil(max(planned, done) / step) * step)`.
findings.scenario: weekly_stat portfolio row for W42 has planned 60, done 52 → the Done line and marker are drawn above the top gridline labelled 40 and overlap the card head

findings.message: The phase tabs link to `/delivery/proposals/<phase>` without the `project` query, so choosing a phase silently drops the project filter that the board's Proposals tab and the Filter menu set. Fix: carry `searchParams.project` into the seg hrefs, as `href()` already does for paging.
findings.scenario: /delivery/proposals?project=CON → click 'Building' → table lists building proposals of every project

findings.message: The page number is never clamped to the row count. An out-of-range `?page=` shows an empty table with an impossible range label and only a 'Previous' link. Fix: clamp the page to `ceil(rows.length / PAGE)`.
findings.scenario: 5 proposals, ?page=10 → empty tbody and label '46–5 of 5'

findings.message: 'planned' was removed from FILTERS, so the Planned lane has no tab, although `/delivery/proposals/planned` still works and the phase card lists Planned. If the mock really omits it, note that in the README.
findings.scenario: User wants planned proposals → no tab to reach them

findings.message: `.seg button[aria-pressed="true"],.tabs [aria-pressed],.tabs [aria-current]` is declared twice: once near the top with `color:var(--chip-agent)` and again here with `color:var(--violet)`. The later rule wins, so the first is dead. Keep one rule.

'amx' depends on 'visual', and 'screens'/'writes' depend on 'amx'. A pixel-diff miss in the visual test therefore skips every functional signed-in suite (auth, delivery, ai, mcp, chat, releases), so a visual regression hides their results. Consider seeding AMX in a way that doesn't make the functional suites depend on the visual one passing (e.g. a setup project that always runs).
findings.scenario: One region diffs 2.5% → visual fails → auth/delivery/chat/releases specs report 'did not run'

findings.message: The test title says 'each region within 2%', but ALLOW raises five regions to 3–4%. Also, `got.count() >= n` leaves extra app regions beyond the mock's count unchecked. Make the title say that allowances exist, and record the waived regions against AC-6 in the change record.
The comment says 'The Active map is the mock's four', but the assertion expects three releases. Fix whichever one is wrong.

The pins 'Tasks done per week' and 'Revenue by project' point at `list_projects`, and 'Shipped to Prod per week' (ProposalsPage) points at `list_proposals`. A pinned chart therefore gives chat a different dataset than the one shown. Add read tools for the weekly series, or label the pins for what they actually carry.
findings.scenario: Pin 'Tasks done per week' and ask amax about last week's throughput → chat receives the project list, not the weekly numbers

findings.message: The fixtures now deviate from fixtures.md (Login hotfix moved from HRI to FLT, new older releases, shipped series W41 1 / W42 0). The deviation is documented only in the module README, while fixtures.md stays unchanged. Record it in fixtures.md (or the 041 change record) so the two sources agree.

The clock pin moved 'today' for the windows but did not bound them at today. phaseCounts counts released_at >= the 1st of the pinned month with no upper bound, and shippedPerWeek has no upper bound either. As soon as a tenant's pin is earlier than real time, releases after the pin are counted. weeklyThroughput is not affected because it matches weeks exactly. Fix: add `released_at < <start of next month>` to phaseCounts (and `< next Monday` to shippedPerWeek), and add a test with a pin earlier than a recorded release.
findings.scenario: Pin the tenant to 2026-09-15 and release a proposal to Prod on 2026-10-01 → 'Released this month' (September) counts the October release.

findings.message: The Sprint select is inert: it has one option and no handler, so it looks like a control that does nothing. Show the sprint as text until sprint switching exists.
findings.scenario: Open /delivery/p/CON and use the Sprint select → nothing changes.

findings.message: Avatars are keyed by initials only, so two different people with the same initials get the same illustrated face. Key the face on a person id, or fall back to plain initials when a name is not in the fixture set.
findings.scenario: A new user 'Nadia Senanayake' (NS) owns a card → it shows Nimal Silva's bearded face.
